components.name: Corner Bracket
components.description: Drawn schematic-style corner marks framing a section.
components.css: .ds-bracket { position: relative; } .ds-bracket::before, .ds-bracket::after { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-top: 2px solid #111111; border-left: 2px solid #111111; top: 0; left: 0; } .ds-bracket::after { top: auto; left: auto; bottom: 0; right: 0; border: none; border-bottom: 2px solid #111111; border-right: 2px solid #111111; }

narrative.overview: The design blog's own illustration language — schematics, connectors, annotations — is amplified from one section into the page's dominant structural device.
keyCharacteristics: Every section boundary is a drawn corner-bracket
Thin connector lines link related concepts across sections
The dark surface is a deliberate 'diagram canvas', not drift
Annotation captions with leader lines appear on hero and feature art

rules.name: The One-Diagram-Language Rule
rules.body: Every illustration on the page uses the same schematic vocabulary — no section gets a different illustration style.

dos: Apply the schematic vocabulary to every section.
Treat the dark surface as an intentional, named diagram canvas.
donts: Don't introduce any color or font outside the captured surface.
Don't let brackets/connectors become decorative — every mark must annotate something real.
